mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% over the prior quarter reduces discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the last month before the decision date
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or the 5-day moving average of 20-day returns remains non-negative over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by more than 10,000 in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the labor signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE and 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 suggests expanding manufacturing demand, which anticipates a rebound in corporate profits and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when INDPRO is above 105 for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in energy prices (HOUST) below $80 per barrel for two months reduces input costs for energy-dependent firms, lowering their required rate of return and contributing to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses below 80 for the second consecutive month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when HOUST < 80 for the preceding 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates aggressive rate hikes, which elevates borrowing costs and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for at least 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL > 3% for 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a labor market tightening that increases wage growth expectations, raising inflation and compressing equity valuations, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) when UNRATE < 3.5% for 90 days.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in consumer spending (PAYEMS) and retail sales (not in observable list - so skip this) are not possible; instead, a strong demand signal can be proxy by a rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) and residential investment (not available). Instead, use a combined proxy: rising GDPC1 (demand) and rising HOUST (energy demand). When both rise for two months, it signals robust economic momentum that supports positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 crosses above its 12-month moving average and HOUST increases by 5% over the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite both proxies rising for 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock such as a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100, market participants anticipate production constraints, which elevates risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 100 for 15 consecutive days.
